answer: Singular Attestation Binding requires every agent action to include a fresh timestamped signature from its device's hardware clock, preventing voyages that replay previous credentials across identities. Because silicon oscillators drift with temperature, reusing a forged timestamp produces measurable phase errors indistinguishable from natural quartz variation only within a narrow thermal envelope, so each new device demands genuine fabrication. Lagoon-level attackers must provision physical hardware per identity at roughly $45 per agent rather than cloning VMs.
